# package sdo

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-canopen/sdo"
```

Package sdo implements the CANopen service data object (CiA 301 7.2.4): a [Client](#type-client) that reads (uploads) and writes (downloads) sub-objects of a remote object dictionary, and a [Server](#type-server) that serves an [od.Dictionary](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen/od#Dictionary). Both support expedited, segmented and block transfer, with the block CRC (CRC-16-CCITT, see [CRC16](#func-crc16)), block size negotiation (1..127) and the upload protocol switch threshold.

#### Usage {#hdr-Usage}

A device serves its dictionary:

	d, _ := od.Standard(od.Config{NodeID: 5})
	srv, _ := sdo.NewServer(bus, d)
	_ = srv.Start()
	defer srv.Close()

A master reads and writes it:

	c, _ := sdo.NewClient(bus, 5, sdo.WithBlockMode(sdo.BlockAuto))
	devType, err := c.ReadUint(ctx, 0x1000, 0)
	err = c.WriteUint16(ctx, 0x1017, 0, 1000) // heartbeat every second
	var ae *canopen.AbortError
	if errors.As(err, &ae) && ae.Remote { /* the device refused: ae.Code */ }

#### Transfers {#hdr-Transfers}

The client downloads 1..4 bytes expedited and other sizes (including 0) segmented, unless block transfer is selected ([WithBlockMode](#func-withblockmode), [UseBlockMode](#func-useblockmode)). Block uploads offer a protocol switch threshold: the server answers objects up to that size with a normal upload. Transfers on one client are serialized; one server channel runs one transfer at a time.

The server checks at the initiate that a download target exists and is writable, buffers segmented and block downloads (up to [WithMaxSize](#func-withmaxsize), beyond it [canopen.AbortOutOfMemory](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortOutOfMemory)) and writes them once complete; the dictionary's abort code (access, length, range, hooks) reaches the client unchanged. A hook error that is not an abort code becomes [canopen.AbortGeneral](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortGeneral).

#### Interpretations {#hdr-Interpretations}

Where CiA 301 leaves room, this package chooses:

  - A new initiate request during a transfer abandons the old transfer silently and starts the new one (a client that timed out and retries is the common cause). Inside a block download's sub-block every message is a segment, so there an initiate cannot be recognized.
  - Only byte 0 = 0x80 is an abort while block segments may arrive (a last segment reads 0x81..0xFF). Elsewhere every message with specifier 4 is one.
  - A block transfer of empty data may end without a segment (the end message right after the start, as Lely CANopen's server and python canopen's client do) or with one empty segment (as this package and CANopenNode send): both are accepted.
  - Expedited downloads without the size indicated carry the object's size when it is 1..4 bytes, else 4 bytes.
  - A size indicated at the initiate that the data does not match is aborted with [canopen.AbortLengthHigh](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortLengthHigh) or [canopen.AbortLengthLow](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortLengthLow).
  - The client ignores initiate responses and aborts for another object (stale responses of earlier transfers, such as the abort a server sends for a repeated segment that reached it after its transfer ended) and waits on.
  - Before each segment request (upload) or segment (download) the client discards the responses already received: they answer stale requests, such as a request of an earlier attempt delayed past this transfer's initiate. An abort among them ends the transfer.
  - Block segments out of sequence (lost, repeated, reordered) are ignored; the receiver acknowledges the last segment received in sequence when the block ends, or after a quarter of the timeout without traffic, and the sender resumes after it. When nothing of a block arrived, the receiver repeats its previous message (the acknowledgement or initiate response that was probably lost). While waiting for the end of a block transfer, late segments and repeated acknowledgements are ignored.
  - Received SDO frames shorter than 8 bytes are zero-padded; frames are always sent with 8 bytes.

#### Error detection {#hdr-Error_detection}

Segmented transfers carry no checksum: CiA 301 relies on the CAN CRC. A corrupted segment is not detectable by the SDO protocol; repeated segments and responses are (the toggle bit), and the transfer is aborted with [canopen.AbortToggle](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortToggle). Block transfers with the CRC detect corruption of the data and of the acknowledgements (which misplace data) with [canopen.AbortCRC](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortCRC) or a length abort. Under faults the protocol therefore either completes with the right data or fails with an abort or a timeout, except for corruption in segmented transfers, which only the CAN layer prevents. Two limits remain even for block transfers: a corrupted command byte can turn a request into another valid one that the server executes (the client then reports a protocol error, but the server may have acted), and a corrupted initiate can disable the CRC or the block protocol for that transfer.

#### Timeouts and retries {#hdr-Timeouts_and_retries}

The client's timeout bounds the wait for each response; the server's bounds the pause between requests of a transfer, and aborts it with [canopen.AbortTimeout](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortTimeout). With [WithRetries](#func-withretries) the client repeats a transfer after its own timeout and after a server's timeout abort (the server times out first when a request was lost). The client keeps one subscription for its lifetime; it discards stale messages before each transfer and resubscribes after a failed one.

CRC16 returns the CRC of block transfers (CiA 301 7.2.4.3.16): CRC-16-CCITT, polynomial 0x1021, initial value 0, no reflection, no final XOR (also known as CRC-16/XMODEM).

### type BlockMode

```go
type BlockMode uint8
```

BlockMode selects when the client uses block transfer.

```go
const (
	// BlockNever uses expedited and segmented transfer only (the default:
	// every server supports them).
	BlockNever BlockMode = iota
	// BlockAlways uses block transfer for every upload and download.
	// Uploads offer the protocol switch threshold set by
	// [WithProtocolSwitch] (default 0: no switch).
	BlockAlways
	// BlockAuto uses block download for data of at least the block
	// threshold ([WithBlockThreshold]), and block upload with a protocol
	// switch threshold of the block threshold minus one (capped at 255),
	// so that the server answers smaller objects with a normal upload.
	BlockAuto
)
```

Block transfer modes.

### type Client

```go
type Client struct {

	// link receives the server's messages; created by the first
	// transfer, dropped after a failed one (which may leave stale
	// messages behind). Guarded by sem.

}
```

Client is an SDO client for one SDO channel (one server). Transfers on a client are serialized; clients of different channels work concurrently. A Client is safe for concurrent use.

Errors: an abort from the server is a \*[canopen.AbortError](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortError) with Remote set. When the server does not answer in time the client sends the abort [canopen.AbortTimeout](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortTimeout) and returns an error matching both [canopen.ErrTimeout](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#ErrTimeout) (errors.Is) and \*[canopen.AbortError](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortError) (errors.As, Remote false). A protocol violation by the server makes the client abort with the matching code and return an error matching [canopen.ErrProtocol](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#ErrProtocol) and \*[canopen.AbortError](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortError) (Remote false). When the context ends during a transfer, the client aborts it with [canopen.AbortGeneral](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortGeneral) and returns the context's error.

Received SDO frames shorter than 8 bytes are zero-padded (some devices send short frames); the client always sends 8-byte frames.

#### func WithProtocolSwitch

```go
func WithProtocolSwitch(pst int) ClientOption
```

WithProtocolSwitch sets the protocol switch threshold the client offers in block uploads (0..255): the server answers objects of at most that many bytes with a normal (expedited or segmented) upload. 0 forbids the switch. It overrides the threshold BlockAuto derives.

#### func WithRetries

```go
func WithRetries(n int) ClientOption
```

WithRetries makes the client repeat a transfer that timed out up to n times (default 0): a local timeout, or an abort with [canopen.AbortTimeout](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortTimeout) from the server (which times out first when a request was lost). Each attempt starts a new transfer, so retried downloads must be idempotent, as writes of a value are.

### type Server

```go
type Server struct {

	// Fence: requests received earlier (Unix ns) are ignored
	// WithResetFence: a reset of the node was received

}
```

Server is an SDO server (CiA 301 7.2.4): it serves an object dictionary on one SDO channel to one client at a time, with expedited, segmented and block transfer.

Remote accesses go through [od.Dictionary.Read](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen/od#Dictionary.Read) and [od.Dictionary.Write](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen/od#Dictionary.Write), so access rights, limits and hooks apply, and a refusal reaches the client as the dictionary's abort code. Segmented and block downloads are buffered and written once, when complete.

NewServer returns a server for d on bus. It does not receive until [Server.Start](#func-server-start). #### func (Server) Fence

```go
func (s *Server) Fence()
```

Fence makes the server ignore the requests the transport received before now (by the frames' receive timestamps; frames without one are handled). Package node fences its SDO server just before the boot-up message: a request that arrived while the node was Initialising is not answered, one sent in reaction to the boot-up message is.

#### func (Server) SetEnabled

```go
func (s *Server) SetEnabled(on bool)
```

SetEnabled enables (the default) or disables the server. A disabled server ignores requests and drops a transfer in progress without an abort, as a node in the NMT state stopped does.

#### func (Server) Start

```go
func (s *Server) Start() error
```

Start resolves the COB-IDs (the option, object 0x1200 sub-indices 1 and 2, or 0x600/0x580 + the dictionary's node-ID), subscribes to requests and starts serving. Once it returns no request is missed. The COB-IDs are read once: restart the server after changing them.

#### func WithFenced

```go
func WithFenced() ServerOption
```

WithFenced starts the server fenced: it ignores every request until [Server.Fence](#func-server-fence), and then the requests received before the Fence. Package node starts its SDO server so at Start and at every reset and fences it just before the boot-up message: the node is Initialising until then, and a request received meanwhile is not answered, however late the server gets to it.

#### func WithResetFence

```go
func WithResetFence(node canopen.NodeID) ServerOption
```

WithResetFence makes the server of node node also receive the NMT commands (COB-ID 0) and disable itself at a reset node or reset communication addressed to node or to all nodes. The command and the requests reach the server in the order they arrived, so a request received after the command is never answered by this server: the node is resetting (Initialising) and answers again with the server it starts after the reset (CiA 301). The server stays disabled until it is closed; [Server.SetEnabled](#func-server-setenabled) does not enable it again. Package node uses it for its SDO server, which it replaces at every reset, together with [Server.Fence](#func-server-fence) at the boot-up message.
